q: What is the vector address (in the interrupt vector table) of INT 21H in the 8086?
exp: Vector address = type number x 4 = 21H x 4 = 84H.

q: Which 8085 instruction is used to mask the RST 5.5, 6.5 and 7.5 interrupts selectively?
exp: SIM (Set Interrupt Mask) uses the accumulator bits to set or reset the individual RST mask bits; RIM only reads them.

q: In an 8051 program, A = 50H and B = 04H and MUL AB is executed. The result is
exp: 80 x 4 = 320 = 0140H; low byte 40H goes to A, high byte 01H to B, and OV = 1 because the product exceeds 255.

q: Match the devices: (i) 8255 (ii) 8253 (iii) 8259 (iv) 8279 with (a) programmable interval timer (b) programmable peripheral interface (c) keyboard/display controller (d) programmable interrupt controller.
exp: 8255 is the PPI, 8253 the timer, 8259 the interrupt controller and 8279 the keyboard/display interface.

q: In the 8086, which register serves as the count register for the LOOP instruction?
exp: CX is the count register used by LOOP, REP and shift/rotate counts (CL).

q: After reset, the 8051 stack pointer and program counter contain
exp: Reset sets PC = 0000H and SP = 07H, so the first PUSH stores data at 08H.

q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the standard 8051?
exp: The standard 8051 has no on-chip ADC; one must be interfaced externally.

q: In an 8085 program, MVI A,0FFH is followed by INR A (CY was 0 before). The Zero and Carry flags are
exp: FFH + 1 = 00H so Z = 1; INR does not affect the carry flag, so CY stays 0.

q: In a microcontroller-based temperature measurement system the ADC is used to
options: convert digital values to analog voltages
convert the analog sensor voltage into a digital number
exp: An analog-to-digital converter digitises the sensor output so the CPU can process it.

q: Which bus of a microprocessor system is bidirectional?
exp: Data travels both to and from the CPU on the data bus, while the address bus is unidirectional (CPU to memory/I/O).

q: The 8086 string instruction MOVSB copies a byte
exp: MOVSB copies the byte at DS:SI to ES:DI and then adjusts SI and DI according to DF.

q: Timer 1 of the 8051 is used in Mode 2 to overflow after 100 pulses. The value loaded in TH1 is
A master 8259A with all its eight IR inputs connected to slave 8259As can handle at most how many interrupt levels?
exp: 8 slaves x 8 inputs = 64 interrupt levels (the master's inputs are used for the slaves).

q: Which memory type is commonly used to store firmware in modern microcontrollers and can be electrically erased block by block?
exp: Flash is non-volatile and electrically erasable in blocks, so firmware can be updated in-system.

q: Setting the trap flag (TF) of the 8086 causes
options: a single-step interrupt after every instruction
exp: With TF = 1 the processor generates a type-1 interrupt after each instruction, which is used for debugging.

q: Pins P3.2 and P3.3 of the 8051 have the alternate functions
exp: P3.0 RXD, P3.1 TXD, P3.2 INT0, P3.3 INT1, P3.4 T0, P3.5 T1, P3.6 WR, P3.7 RD.

q: In an 8085 program A = 30H and B = 40H and CMP B is executed. The flags are
exp: CMP subtracts B from A without storing: A < B so a borrow occurs (CY = 1) and the result is non-zero (Z = 0).

q: The 8255 is loaded with control word 83H. Which port configuration results?
options: Port A input, Port B output, Port C input
Port A output, Port B input, upper C output, lower C input
Port A input, Port B input, Port C output
exp: 83H = 1000 0011: A output, upper C output, Mode 0 for B, B input, lower C input.

q:
Statement I: In I/O-mapped I/O the whole memory address space is available for memory.
Statement II: In I/O-mapped I/O arithmetic and logical instructions can be applied directly to I/O devices.
Which is correct?
exp: I/O-mapped I/O uses a separate address space so memory is not reduced (I true), but only IN/OUT can access ports (II is a feature of memory-mapped I/O).

q: An 8051 is driven by a 12 MHz crystal. The duration of one machine cycle is
exp: One machine cycle = 12 oscillator periods = 12 / 12 MHz = 1 microsecond.

q: In an 8086 with SS = 3000H and SP = 0100H, PUSH AX is executed. At which physical address is AH stored?
exp: SP becomes 00FEH; the high byte AH is stored at SP+1 = 00FFH (physical 300FFH) and AL at 300FEH.

q: The 8085 flag register contains only the Zero and Carry flags set. Its value is
exp: Flag format S Z X AC X P X CY (D7-D0): Z = D6 and CY = D0, giving 0100 0001 = 41H.

q: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) in a microcontroller is commonly used to
options: control motor speed or LED brightness
exp: Varying the duty cycle of a fixed-frequency pulse varies the average power delivered to a motor or LED.

q: The serial I/O lines of the 8085 are
exp: SID (serial input data) and SOD (serial output data) are used with the RIM and SIM instructions.

q: To transfer a 16-bit word starting at an even address, the 8086 makes BHE and A0 respectively
exp: BHE = 0 enables the upper half of the data bus and A0 = 0 enables the lower half, so both bytes transfer in one cycle.

q: The bit-addressable area of the 8051 internal RAM lies at addresses
exp: 16 bytes from 20H to 2FH give 128 individually addressable bits (00H-7FH).

q: In the 8085 the ALE signal is used to
options: latch the lower address byte from the multiplexed AD0-AD7 lines
exp: ALE goes high at the start of a machine cycle so an external latch (e.g. 74LS373) can capture A0-A7.

q: Which 8253 mode is called 'interrupt on terminal count'?
exp: In Mode 0 the output goes high when the count reaches zero and is used to raise an interrupt.

q: An 8051 executes MOV A,#3CH then SWAP A then ADD A,#05H. The accumulator contains
exp: SWAP exchanges nibbles: 3CH becomes C3H; adding 05H gives C8H.

q: Which bit position of the 8086 flag register holds the Overflow flag (OF)?
exp: OF is bit D11; DF is D10, IF is D9 and SF is D7.

q: Compared with a general-purpose microprocessor, a microcontroller typically has
options: higher clock speed and large external memory support only
an instruction set designed mainly for number crunching
lower cost and power with bit-oriented instructions for control tasks
exp: Microcontrollers target dedicated control with on-chip peripherals and bit-manipulation instructions at low cost and power.

q: The 8085 instruction RST 3 transfers control to which address?
exp: RST n jumps to 8 x n; for n = 3 this is 18H.

q: Which flag in the 8051 PSW reflects the parity of the accumulator?
exp: The P flag (PSW.0) is set when the accumulator contains an odd number of 1 bits.

q: In an 8086 program, MOV AL,0FFH is followed by ADD AL,01H. The Carry and Zero flags are
exp: FFH + 01H = 100H: the 8-bit result 00H gives ZF = 1 and the carry out of bit 7 sets CF = 1.
